title: The Mildred Bailey Show incident and CBS firing the trumpets
summary: CBS fired all 13 trumpet players after the incident and rehired all but Maxwell.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: couple years, when that incident came up that I mentioned earlier about hiring the black musicians on the Mildred Bailey Show. That was -- well, that was not really sponsored but it was an outside show, what they call outside. They hired musicians other than the staff musicians. I think the only staff musicians on that show was Specs Powell and myself. Specs Powell, the drummer, you remember him?
And then the rest was people like Teddy Wilson, Al Hall, Roy Eldridge, Charlie Shavers, Willie Smith, Ben Webster, Trummy Young, Will Bradley, Billy Butterfield for a while.
That was considered an outside show?

Yes, and we were paid extra for that. Well, shortly after that incident, you know, they said that they were not going to retaliate against me in any way, so what CBS did was it fired all 13 trumpet players that were on the staff. And no trumpet players left. And then a few weeks later hired everybody back except me.
But by that time I had gone on to the Perry Como Show so I didn't care. I didn't make waves, you know, I'd made my point. I didn't care.
